market_name: Will North Korea invade South Korea before 2027?

time_plan.30m: Check whether the Polymarket probability move is sustained or a single-print spike; scan newswires (Yonhap, Reuters) for any DMZ/artillery/mobilization headlines; check EWY pre/after-hours and KOSPI futures.
time_plan.1h: Confirm if KRW (USDKRW) and KOSPI futures corroborate the stress; distinguish real escalation from market noise or a large speculative bet.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether official sources (South Korea MND, US Forces Korea, UN) have commented; gauge whether safe-haven flows (gold, USD, JGBs) are also firing.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether the move has broadened to Japan (EWJ) and regional risk; check if the prediction-market move has reverted, suggesting a false signal.
time_plan.12h: Mark EWY return vs. entry; determine if the leak preceded any public confirmation or fully reversed, and log calibration outcome.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp upward move in the implied probability of a North Korean invasion would signal rising Korean Peninsula conflict risk. South Korean equities are the most directly exposed liquid asset: war risk crushes valuations, hits exporters, and triggers capital flight. EWY is the deepest US-listed proxy for the KOSPI. The move is asymmetric — this is a persistent near-zero-probability tail, so any genuine jump in the market implies a material, under-priced escalation, which would produce an outsized equity selloff.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm the prediction-market jump is real; check spot gold and GLD for any immediate bid.
time_plan.1h: Watch whether USD, JPY, and Treasuries also catch a bid, confirming a genuine risk-off impulse rather than idiosyncratic noise.
time_plan.2h: Assess magnitude — gold often needs confirmed escalation to move meaningfully; downgrade if no corroboration.
time_plan.6h: Check if gold move persists or fades as headlines clarify; compare to EWY move for internal consistency.
time_plan.12h: Record GLD return vs. entry and whether safe-haven thesis held or the signal was noise.

predictions.reasoning: A credible rise in Korean war-risk probability would drive safe-haven demand into gold, USD, and Treasuries. Gold is a liquid, globally traded hedge against geopolitical shock. However, the mapping is weaker and smaller than the Korea-equity link because gold responds to a broad basket of global risks and a single regional scare may not move it much unless escalation looks imminent.

evidence_used: Market question concerns a binary tail-risk event (NK invasion of SK before 2027) in the military_conflict category, Korea region
Resolution relies on official confirmation or credible-reporting consensus — a genuine escalation would be a major market-moving public event
South Korean equities (KOSPI/EWY) are the most directly exposed liquid asset to Korean Peninsula conflict
Safe-haven assets (gold, USD, Treasuries) historically rally on geopolitical war scares
uncertainty_notes: This is a persistent near-zero-probability tail; most probability moves are likely speculative noise or thin-liquidity prints rather than real information
A probability move without corroborating newswire or FX/futures confirmation is probably a false signal
The 12h window may not capture the asset reaction if the leak precedes public confirmation by days
Magnitude estimates assume a genuine, sizeable escalation signal — a minor probability tick would imply near-zero asset move

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a North Korean invasion of South Korea would signal rising Korean Peninsula conflict risk. The cleanest, most liquid public-market expression is a selloff in South Korean equities (EWY), with a secondary safe-haven bid in gold (GLD). The equity link is strong and directionally reliable; the gold link is weaker and smaller. Because this is a persistent tail-risk market, the dominant caveat is that most probability moves are noise — only a sustained move corroborated by newswires and FX/futures should be treated as a real signal.
key_assumptions: A material upward move in the market's implied probability reflects genuine escalation information, not thin-market noise
South Korean equity and KRW markets are open or have tradable proxies (EWY, USDKRW) during the window
The escalation signal is not already fully priced into Korean assets
failure_modes: The probability move is a single large speculative bet or low-liquidity artifact that reverts, with no real asset impact
The event is already public, so EWY and gold have already repriced before the prediction-market signal
GLD is a weak proxy — gold responds to many global factors and may not move on a single regional scare
Korean markets or ETF trading are closed/illiquid during the window, muting or delaying the measurable move
Base rate is extremely low; even a notable probability jump may still imply a tiny absolute risk, producing sub-threshold asset moves
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
